title: service-tier-uptake-sensitivity-hiring-corridor-projection
summary: Working analysis to map how small shifts in service-tier adoption (Free / Standard / Enterprise) change hiring corridors, monthly burn, and projected runway. Intended as an operational playbook for the FP&A and GTM teams during the Q4 planning window.
assumptions: Baseline ARR composition (as of 2026-10-31): Free 45%, Standard 40%, Enterprise 15%
Average revenue per account (ARPA) by tier: Free $0, Standard $1,200/mo, Enterprise $18,000/mo
Unit economics: marginal gross margin on incremental Standard seat = 78%, Enterprise seat = 65% (includes support/SLA uplift)
Hiring cadence: 1 IC eng = $18k/month fully-burdened; Sales AE = $14k/month fully-burdened; Solutions Eng = $16k/month fully-burdened
No material pricing changes applied in baseline; sensitivity applies % uplift or downgrade to published list price
scenarios: Conservative: Standard uptake -2pp, Enterprise uptake +1pp (users downgrade to avoid price increases)
Base: status quo adoption (no SKU mix shift)
Growth: Standard +3pp, Enterprise +2pp (improved GTM motions and product-market fit enhancements)
Stress: Enterprise churn -3pp, Standard -5pp (macro hit to large deals and stickiness)
Price-shock: +10% list price on Standard with 0-20% elasticity applied across scenarios
headcount_plan_summary: We define a flexible hiring corridor: minimum run-rate hiring (freeze non-critical roles) preserves runway by +4 months vs baseline; aggressive hiring (full plan: +18 hires over 12 months, weighted to infra and SRE) shortens runway by ~3 months under Stress scenario. Recommended phased hires: Q1 focus on GTM (4 AEs) to pursue Standard uplift; Q2-Q3 engineering hires gated on realized revenue uplift from tier shifts.
pricing_sensitivity_summary: Small price moves on Standard materially change unit revenues: a 5% price increase with assumed 3% elasticity yields +1.5% net revenue vs baseline but amplifies churn risk for price-sensitive mid-market customers. Enterprise price actions have lower elasticity but higher absolute effect per account. Net margin sensitivity curve attached in linked artifacts.
runway_impact_estimate: Baseline runway (no changes) = 14.2 months. Conservative scenario extends runway to 15.1 months (lower hiring), Growth reduces to 13.0 months if hiring accelerates without immediate ARR realization, Stress reduces runway to 10.8 months. Price-shock downside case (10% raise, 12% churn elasticity) reduces runway by 2.4 months.
decision_triggers: Metric: 8-week rolling net new Standard ARR < -2% => pause non-essential engineering hires
Metric: Enterprise net retention < 94% over a quarter => activate contingency hiring freeze and reprioritize support resources
Metric: Conversion from Free->Standard improves by >20% QoQ => greenlight next tranche of GTM hires
Finance guardrail: Cash balance forecast below 9 months => initiate hiring corridor to minimum staffing plan

GTM to run 6-week price experiment on new Standard bundles with limited cohort and report elasticity - owner: Aisha Gomez
People Ops to prepare two offer windows with conservative and aggressive hiring packages (draft by 2026-11-20)
Product to deliver telemetry signal for Free->Standard trial conversion and report cohort LTV (deliverable: 2026-12-15)
Treasury: stress-test cash runway under Stress + Price-shock scenarios and recommend minimum commit levels to ops (due 2026-11-18)
notes: This doc is intentionally conservative in assumptions for hiring costs and ramp time. Use primarily as a gating instrument for Q1 hiring approvals. Open questions: (1) precise elasticity by subsegment within Standard (PLG self-serve vs assisted), (2) lead time on Enterprise renewals that could mask churn velocity. Follow-ups scheduled with Revenue Ops and Research on 2026-11-12.
